hook: Colin Raffel studied at Columbia University, where his early research focused on music information retrieval, before joining Google Brain as a research scientist. There he led the team that published Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer, introducing the T5 model and its text-to-text framing of natural language processing tasks, later published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research. He subsequently moved into academia, and today he is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at the University of Toronto, an Associate Research Director at the Vector Institute, and a Faculty Researcher at Hugging Face. His current research group focuses on decentralizing, democratizing, and de-risking large-scale AI, including work on collaborative and communication-efficient training methods.
